review.notes: Structure pass over the whole Markdown (single balanced python fence pair; no swallowed blocks) plus a normalized whole-document text diff of all 59 physical PDF pages against the OCR Markdown, followed by targeted token-level checks (words >=5 chars, numbers >=3 digits) per page; flagged spots were verified on rendered pages 1, 6, 15 and 47 (300 dpi crops). Pages 7 and 44-48 are dense result tables whose flat text order differs from the Markdown table structure; word/number token-presence checks found no dropped table rows or values there. Figure-internal prompt/response text (Figures 1 and 15) is embedded as images and was not treated as text defects.

patches.evidence: Rendered physical p.1 prints a footnote block under a rule: "Corresponding author(s): lbeyer,xzhai@google.com" followed by "© 2024 Google DeepMind. All rights reserved" (visually verified at 250 dpi). Both lines were dropped by the OCR right after the "*Core team, †Project lead" footnote.

Rendered physical p.6 (300 dpi crop) shows the pretraining-task list of Section 3.2.5: each task prompt such as "caption {lang}", "ocr", "answer en {question}" is a monospace label on its own line, not a section heading. The OCR promoted the first task label to a level-2 heading while its sibling labels stayed plain text.

Rendered physical p.6 (300 dpi crop) shows a task label "ocr" in monospace on its own line directly above the description beginning "Concatenation (in raster order) of all text on the image transcribed by a public OCR system."; the OCR dropped the label, leaving that description orphaned between the caption and answer task descriptions.

Rendered physical p.15 (300 dpi crop of reference [16]) prints "Balitmore, MA, July 2022" — the source's own misspelling of Baltimore, which the OCR silently corrected. The print's spelling is restored; reference [61] on a later page prints "Baltimore, Maryland" correctly and is untouched.

Rendered physical p.47 caption of Table 5 reads "... with 8 devices (4 chips), prefilling 512 tokens, cache sized 640 tokens." (visually verified at 250 dpi); the OCR misread "prefilling" as "prefetching".

unresolved.evidence: In the Section 3.2.5 task list the labels "question {lang} {English answer}", "segment {thing} ; {thing} ; ..." and "caption <ymin><xmin><ymax><xmax>" were merged onto the same line as their descriptions, while sibling labels kept their own line; content is complete, only the line structure differs from the print.
